summary: Colville Reservation lookout: an L-4 cab from 1935, a 1968 timber tower, and the present 53-foot steel live-in tower built 1986; staffed in summer, reached by permit.

access.note: On Colville Indian Reservation land. Non-tribal visitors need a Colville Tribes Reservation Use Pass: $80 a year or $20 a day, good for two vehicles. The tribal sheet is undated, so check current prices.

visit.trail_note: Drive from Omak on Highway 155, then Omak Lookout Road. A high-clearance all-wheel-drive vehicle can reach the summit, but the road is very rocky about 2.5 miles from the top. The tower is a working, staffed lookout.

events.note: First lookout, an L-4 cab, built by the Civilian Conservation Corps.
A July 1943 Colville newspaper item reported teachers working as fire lookouts that summer, including Rachel Butte of Chewelah Junior High on Omak Mountain.
Dorothy Bissell is listed as a lookout.
Eleanor Brown is listed as a lookout.
Inspection report: the 1935 cabin was in poor condition; a new cabin fifteen feet higher was proposed. A television reflector station and Border Patrol building on the site obstructed the view.
A 20-foot timber tower with an R-6 flat cab replaced the original L-4 cab.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on April 13, 2022.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1935 date is the first L-4 cab on the summit. The 1986 date is the present 53-foot tower. The sources differ because they describe different structures, not because one is wrong.
The record lists the design as R-6. The R-6 flat cab was the 1968 cab on a 20-foot timber tower. The tower standing today is the 1986 steel tower.

The register and firelookout.com say the tower is staffed each summer. TrailChick says staffing runs during times of high fire danger. Two sources name summer as the season, and TrailChick ties staffing to high fire danger, so how often someone is up there is unclear.

notes_for_editor: Record lists design R-6, but the R-6 cab was replaced in 1986 by the present 53-foot steel tower; the record's design field may need a human look (not put in corrections because design is not a listed correction field). The tribal permit sheet is undated and the TrailChick road and fee notes come from a 2018 visit with a 2024 update, so confirm the permit price before publishing. The register has a 1952 photo credited to the Washington Digital Archives, not added because no image URL was read. The 1960 inspection report is a Forest Lookouts of Washington transcription, not the original document.
